content.introduction: According to the sources, Tom Lee, chairman of Bitmine Immersion Technologies, has issued warnings about potential sell-offs in Ethereum and the broader crypto market. Specifically, Lee has highlighted the implications of a sell-off in South Korea's tech sector, which could lead to forced liquidations and secondary sell-offs in crypto markets. Additionally, Bitmine has been actively staking Ethereum, increasing its total staked position to approximately 5.67 million ETH, controlling 4.7% of the network. Lee also confirmed that BitMine will not accumulate more than 5% of Ethereum's supply.

According to Tom Lee, chairman of Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) treasury company Bitmine Immersion Technologies (NYSE: BMNR), this sell-off has huge potential implications for crypto. Most notably, it could lead to a sell-off in Ethereum, the one digital asset that his company has been hoarding since June 2025. [...] That's where crypto enters the picture. South Korea is a hotbed of crypto activity, and many tech investors there are also crypto investors. Thus, some investors could be forced to sell off their crypto holdings, partly as a way to make up for the losses now being incurred on their tech stock holdings.

Person in office at night, staring at trading screens.

Image source: Getty Images. [...] On the surface, there might not be a clear connection between Ethereum and what's happening in South Korea and other Asian markets. Here's the thing: The overseas tech sell-off has already resulted in forced liquidations. In turn, says Lee, this activity could lead to a wave of "secondary" liquidations.
